{{ElectionsNH}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in New Hampshire''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[New Hampshire]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] congressman [[Chris Pappas (American politician)|Chris Pappas]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former senator [[John E. Sununu|John Sununu]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Democratic incumbent [[Jeanne Shaheen]] is not seeking re-election, after serving three terms.

[[Primary elections]] were held on September 8. Pappas won the Democratic nomination with 65% of the vote against medical scientist Karishma Manzur. Sununu, who held the seat for one term until he was defeated by Shaheen in [[2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2008]], won the Republican nomination with 68.5% of the vote against former Massachusetts senator [[Scott Brown (politician)|Scott Brown]].

This will be the first open Senate election in New Hampshire since [[2010 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2010]]. Republicans have not won a Senate election in New Hampshire since that race.

{{toclimit|3}}

== Background ==
New Hampshire is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|slightly to moderately blue]] state at the federal level, with [[Kamala Harris]] carrying the state by roughly 3 percentage points in the [[2024 United States presidential election in New Hampshire|2024 presidential election]]. The state's congressional delegation has been entirely Democratic since 2017. However, Republicans control the [[Governor of New Hampshire|governorship]], both state legislative chambers, and a majority in the [[Executive Council of New Hampshire|executive council]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-05 |title=New Hampshire keeps all-Democratic delegation with Pappas, Goodlander wins in US House races |url=https://apnews.com/article/new-hampshire-congress-election-2024-b9a8e05a7847c3ba93c424c2094a49a7 |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-06 |title=NH Republicans claim big State House wins and strengthen majorities in House and Senate |url=https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2024-11-06/nh-republicans-claim-big-state-house-wins-and-strengthen-majorities-in-house-and-senate |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=New Hampshire Public Radio |language=en}}</ref>

Shaheen was first elected in [[2008 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2008]], defeating incumbent [[John E. Sununu|John Sununu]] in a rematch of [[2002 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2002]], and was reelected in [[2014 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2014]] and [[2020 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Castronuovo |first=Celine |date=2020-11-04 |title=Shaheen wins reelection in New Hampshire |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/523894-shaheen-wins-reelection-in-new-hampshire/ |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref> Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire since [[2010 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|2010]].<ref>https://rollcall.com/2025/10/22/new-hampshire-john-sununu-race-rating/</ref>
